items.title: Sandflare – I built a sandbox that launches AI agent VMs in ~300ms
items.raw_excerpt: I've been building Sandflare for the past few months — it launches Firecracker microVMs for AI agents in ~300ms cold start. The idea came from running LLM-generated code in production. Docker felt too risky (shared kernel), full VMs too slow (5–10s). Firecracker hits the middle: real VM isolation, fast boot. I also added managed Postgres because almost every agent I built needed persistent state. One call wires a database into a sandbox. There are great tools in this space already (E2B, Modal, Daytona) — I wanted something with batteries-included Postgres, and simpler pricing What I'm trying to figure out: how do I get cold start below 100ms? Currently the bottleneck is the Firecracker API + network setup. Would love to hear from anyone who's pushed Firecracker further. https://sandflare.i

excerpt_i18n.en:
In recent days, TurboQuant has become one of the hottest controversies in the AI academic community. On one side, Google Research has prominently promoted it in a blog post as a "breakthrough" work that significantly reduces the inference costs of large models and is set to debut at ICLR 2026. On the other side, Gao Jianyang, the author of the prior work RaBitQ, has publicly criticized the paper on Zhihu, with his latest post updated in the early hours of March 30. He argues that the paper has serious issues in its method description, theoretical comparisons, and experimental disclosures. This Zhihu post has already garnered nearly 5K likes. In just a few days, the dispute has evolved from a technical discussion into a public tug-of-war over originality, paper narrative, and the academic influence of major tech companies. 

To clarify the issues with TurboQuant, the external criticism of Google in this controversy is not just a vague question of similarity. Public comments have focused on three key points: first, whether TurboQuant deliberately downplays its methodological connection to RaBitQ; second, whether the paper's characterization of RaBitQ's theory as "suboptimal" is justified; and third, whether the experimental comparisons are set up in a way that favors TurboQuant while disadvantaging prior work. These points remain part of an open debate, not an official ruling, but they indicate that this controversy is not merely about a "missing citation" but strikes at the very core of academic research.
excerpt_i18n.es: Estos días, TurboQuant se ha convertido en uno de los debates más candentes en el círculo académico de IA. Por un lado, Google Research publicó un artículo promocionándolo como un trabajo "revolucionario" que reduce significativamente los costes de inferencia de modelos grandes y se presentará en ICLR 2026. Por otro, Gao Jianyang, autor del trabajo previo RaBitQ, criticó duramente en la comunidad como usuario de Zhihu, con su última actualización el 30 de marzo a primera hora, señalando graves problemas en la descripción del método, comparaciones teóricas y divulgación experimental. Su publicación en Zhihu ya ha recibido cerca de 5.000 "me gusta". En pocos días, esta polémica ha ido más allá.

excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past year, a clearer trend in the AI industry has emerged: what truly sets leaders apart is no longer just the superior performance of a single model in a specific capability, but rather who can organize "capabilities" into "tasks" and then solidify these "tasks" into a "system." Technologies once discussed separately—text-to-image, image-to-video, video generation, 3D generation, motion generation—are now being reconsidered under a unified question: if future models go beyond answering questions and generating content to understanding complex intentions, mobilizing multiple capabilities, and achieving end-to-end creation, then the core of large model competition will shift from the models themselves to the overall synergy between models, agents, skills, and application scenarios. Consequently, the real divide in the "world model" race may not lie solely in which model better approximates physical laws or replicates the real world, but in who can first build a functional, callable, and commercially viable full-modal production system. Against this backdrop, Yao Ting, co-founder and CTO of Zhixiang Future, offers a forward-looking perspective on "world models," "full modality," and "agent platforms." Rather than merely debating the merits of video generation capabilities, he focuses on how models can evolve from isolated capabilities into creative foundations, how skills can be efficiently, securely managed, orchestrated, and combined, and how applications, in turn, shape the next iteration of models. This elevates the significance of this dialogue beyond discussing the product roadmap of an AI video company to addressing, on a deeper level, the broader evolution of the field.
excerpt_i18n.es: En el último año, un cambio cada vez más claro en la industria de la IA es que lo que realmente marca la diferencia ya no es solo si un modelo tiene una capacidad individual más fuerte, sino quién puede organizar las "capacidades" en "tareas" y luego consolidar esas "tareas" en un "sistema". Recently, HiDream.ai and Noitom Robotics officially announced a strategic partnership. The two parties will engage in deep collaboration on generating high-quality, large-scale embodied intelligence video data, thereby initiating a new model of exploration to broaden the data entry points for the embodied intelligence industry. High-availability training data is currently a bottleneck in the rapidly developing embodied intelligence sector. Unlike large language models that can access vast amounts of text data, embodied intelligence requires the integration of multimodal data such as visual, motion, and tactile information. Traditional data collection methods are costly and inefficient, making synthetic data crucial. As the industry booms, training data is shifting from small-scale demonstrations to large-scale, deliverable volumes, with data acquisition, structuring, and engineering capabilities now determining system performance limits.

Based on this assessment, HiDream.ai and Noitom Robotics are combining the millimeter-level controllable video generation capabilities of multimodal large models with real data infrastructure. By integrating "real data + generative video data," the collaboration is expected to produce tens of thousands of hours of embodied intelligence video data within the year, opening a new path for scalable supply of high-quality embodied training data urgently needed by the industry.

At the ceremony, Dai Ruoli, founder and CEO of Noitom Robotics, and Mei Tao, founder and CEO of HiDream.ai, were present to witness this significant moment.

Noitom Robotics: Building the Data Foundation for Embodied Intelligence  
Noitom Robotics is a data company focused on the embodied intelligence and humanoid robotics industries, with "data" at its core.
excerpt_i18n.es: Recientemente, HiDream.ai y Noitom Robotics anunciaron oficialmente una colaboración estratégica. Ambas partes llevarán a cabo una cooperación profunda en la generación de datos de video de inteligencia encarnada de alta calidad y a gran escala, explorando así un nuevo modelo para ampliar el acceso a datos en la industria de la inteligencia encarnada. Los datos de entrenamiento altamente utilizables son actualmente un cuello de botella en el rápido desarrollo de la industria de la inteligencia encarnada. A diferencia de los modelos de lenguaje extenso, que pueden obtener grandes cantidades de datos de texto, la inteligencia encarnada requiere la integración de datos multimodales como visión, movimiento y tacto. Los métodos tradicionales de recopilación son costosos y de baja eficiencia, por lo que los datos sintéticos se han convertido en clave. Con el auge de la industria, los datos de entrenamiento están pasando de demostraciones a pequeña escala a volúmenes masivos.

On March 26, 2026, the internationally renowned academic publisher Nature featured Tianli International Holdings Limited (01773.HK) in two in-depth reports within its Nature Index China special issue, systematically presenting the company's exploration in the "AI+Education" field. The special issue was published alongside the main journal and made available on its official website. Structured around technical features and executive interviews, the reports comprehensively depict the exploration of educational AGI within China's K12 education system from three perspectives: philosophy, technological framework, and scale of application. Globally, few cases in basic education have been systematically presented by Nature, and this inclusion signifies that Tianli's AI+Education initiatives have garnered significant attention and recognition from the international academic and educational technology communities.

1. Structural Constraints in Education and the Boundaries of AI Intervention  
Nature's reports point out that traditional education has long been constrained by the tension between "scalable delivery" and "individual differences," rooted in the difficulty of systematically modeling cognitive processes. The evolution of AI is opening new avenues for solutions. Tianli's proposed approach transforms education from a "content delivery problem" into a "cognitive evolution problem." AI is not defined as a replacement for teachers but rather as undertaking structured, repeatable cognitive support tasks, shifting the teaching process from experience-driven to data- and model-driven. Within this framework, education is modeled as a nonlinear system involving individual cognition, learning environments, and strategies, with its evolutionary outcomes manifesting as the formation and updating of cognitive structures.

La edición especial se publicó simultáneamente con la edición principal y se lanzó en el sitio web oficial. Los reportajes, estructurados como perfiles técnicos y entrevistas con altos directivos, desarrollaron una descripción completa de la exploración de la AGI educativa en el sistema educativo chino de K12 desde tres niveles: conceptos, sistema tecnológico y escala de aplicación. En el ámbito de la educación básica global, son pocos los casos que han sido presentados sistemáticamente por Nature, lo que hace que esta selección sea destacable.

items.title: 中山大学梁小丹团队论文：让视频生成从「看起来真实」到「物理上正确」丨CVPR 2026
items.raw_excerpt: 想象这样一些常见却又微妙的场景：一勺蜂蜜缓慢倒入热茶，本应拉出细长连续的丝状流动，但很多生成视频却会突然断裂甚至凭空消失；一块冰在室温下逐渐融化，真实过程应该是边缘先软化、体积变化、最终消散，而生成结果却常常直接从完整变成消失；一个玻璃球落入水中，本应经历接触水面、减速下沉、逐渐稳定的过程，但模型却可能只给出一个结果画面。 这些现象并不罕见，也正是当前视频生成技术最容易让人出戏的地方。画面看起来像，但过程不对，缺乏因果关系，也缺乏真实世界中那种连续演化的逻辑。 随着视频生成模型的发展，从 OpenAI Sora 到 Kling 等系统不断刷新视觉质量的上限，行业已经基本解决了清晰度和风格的问题，却逐渐暴露出更深层的瓶颈，即模型缺乏对物理规律的理解能力。 现有方法更多依赖数据驱动的模式匹配，本质上是在生成看起来合理的结果，而不是在模拟真实发生的过程，这也导致在流体、热变化以及多物体交互等场景中表现明显不足。 在这样的背景下，来自四川大学的雷印杰团队提出了一项新的研究工作《Chain of Event-Centric Causal Thought for Physically Plausible Video Generation》。这项研究不再直接从文本生成视频，而是尝试让模型先理解物理过程本身，将复杂现象拆分为一系列具有因果关系的事件，并结合物理规律进行约束，再逐步生成视频内容。 通过这种方式，目标不再只是让画面看起来真实，而是让变化过程本身也符合现实世界的运行逻辑，从而在更深层次上提升视频生成的可信度和一致性。 论文地址：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.09094 更加符合「真实世界」的方式 在实验结果方面，研究团队首先在 PhyGenBench 数据集上进行了系统评估。这个数据集包含 160 条物理描述，覆盖力学、光学、热学和材料四类典型物理场景。

Imagine some common yet subtle scenarios: a spoonful of honey slowly poured into hot tea should form a long, continuous thread-like flow, but many generated videos show it suddenly breaking or even disappearing out of thin air; an ice cube gradually melting at room temperature should first soften at the edges, change in volume, and eventually dissipate, yet generated results often shift directly from intact to vanished; a glass ball falling into water should go through the process of touching the surface, slowing down as it sinks, and gradually stabilizing, but models may only produce a single outcome frame. These phenomena are not uncommon and are precisely where current video generation technology most easily breaks immersion. The visuals may look similar, but the process is off—lacking causality and the logical continuity of evolution found in the real world.

This leads to noticeable shortcomings in scenarios involving fluids, thermal changes, and multi-object interactions.

excerpt_i18n.en:
Waking up at 3 a.m. may be the most relatable anxiety scenario for contemporary professionals. We try to retrieve the flash of insight from a dinner two hours earlier, only grasping a few vague words—supply chain? Downward market? Neuroscience research shows that without external reinforcement within 30 seconds of an idea's emergence, the loss rate of details can be as high as 70%. However, the real challenge lies not in memory but in the act of recording itself. In business settings—toasting, shaking hands, driving, or networking at exhibitions—"pulling out a phone" is the ultimate social taboo and operational barrier. Countless ideas spark daily in coffee chats and brainstorming sessions, only to be lost on the "path to operational tools."  

The current AI Agent market presents an interesting paradox: the more powerful the technology, the higher the usability barrier. Conversational agents require you to stay by the screen; wearables either listen indiscriminately (a privacy nightmare) or have complex activation processes (an operational burden). Users possess the most powerful AI yet miss opportunities when they need it most, simply because "activating it" is cumbersome.  

"Workplace efficiency has never been built on transcribing text. What we truly need is the ability to execute ideas the moment they are spoken." This is the foundation of Gyges Labs' creation of the Vocci Ring—the world's first AI note-taking ring, offering the shortest path to AI Agent interaction.
excerpt_i18n.es: Despertarse sobresaltado a las tres de la madrugada podría ser la escena de ansiedad más compartida entre los profesionales contemporáneos. Intentamos rescatar en nuestra mente esa chispa de inspiración que surgió durante la cena de negocios dos horas antes, pero solo logramos atrapar unas cuantas palabras difusas: ¿cadena de suministro? ¿mercado de bajos ingresos? La investigación en neurociencia muestra que, si no se consolida externamente en los primeros 30 segundos después de surgir, la tasa de pérdida de detalles de una idea alcanza el 70%. Sin embargo, la verdadera dificultad no radica en la memoria, sino en el acto mismo de registrar. Cuando te encuentras en un entorno empresarial —brindando, estrechando manos, conduciendo, intercambiando saludos en ferias— "sacar el teléfono" se convierte en el mayor tabú social y barrera operativa. A diario, generamos innumerables ideas en conversaciones de café o lluvias de ideas, pero las vemos desvanecerse ante nuestros ojos.
